Hepatoblastoma is a different type of liver tumor, distinct from hemangiosarcoma, which is of vascular origin. The histological description (polygonal to short spindle-shaped cells, dilated sinusoids, local invasion into blood vessels, reticular fibers) is characteristic of hemangiosarcoma, not hepatoblastoma.
Hepatoblastoma (epithelial type) is a different type of liver tumor. The histological features described are not consistent with hepatoblastoma but are characteristic of hemangiosarcoma.

Hepatocellular carcinoma is a different type of liver malignancy arising from hepatocytes. The described histology (spindle-shaped cells, dilated sinusoids, vascular invasion, reticular fibers) is not consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma but points to hemangiosarcoma.
